proposals.evidence: Platts p. 497 identifies Persian khūn “blood”. The distinctive kh/x plus ūn family is retained, separate from inherited lohi/lahu blood words. Existing Hindi khun “blood” (kannauji[p. 60]) supplies an attested provisional donor. Its locality is the attestation site; the historical lending locality and possible intervening Indo-Aryan language remain unknown. The borrowed edge is saved under the user’s explicit preference to link supported families despite unresolved cross-IA transmission.

Existing Hindi sal “year” (kannauji[p. 85]) supplies an attested provisional donor. Its locality is the attestation site; the historical lending locality and possible intervening Indo-Aryan language remain unknown.
